summary: Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn, and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg in 2012 under Harunaga Isaacson. She served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She earned an MA in Buddhist art at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016). She is a professor at Keimyung University.

Junjirō Takakusu (1866–1945) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Leipzig, and Tokyo, and under Friedrich Max Müller, Moriz Winternitz, and Sylvain Lévi. He was a professor (1897–1927) and president (1930–1945) at the University of Tokyo.

Junkei Washio (1868–1941) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Toyo University (c. 1888–1893). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University and Toyo University (c. 1925–1941), and held a post at Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi (b. 1935) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt (c. 1964–1968). He held posts at Hokkaido University (c. 1968–1996), ICPBS (Chancellor, c. 1996–2011), and IIBS (Director, c. 2000–2011).

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at the Australian National University (1980) and doctoral work at the University of Göttingen (1990). In 2011, she was attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Minamoto (b. 1947) works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed a master's course at Ryukoku University, pursued doctoral studies at Otani University (c. 1974–1979), and served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang (1886–1969) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang, at Waseda University (c. 1906–1910), and at Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1913–1915). He held posts at Peking University (c. 1918–1920) and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato (b. 1934) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Catholic University of Louvain and the University of Tokyo (PhD 1986) under Étienne Lamotte, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura. He held professorships at Nishogakusha, Nagoya, and Reitaku.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied at Kansai University and later held academic posts at Ryukoku University (c. 1920–1945) and Kansai University (c. 1948–1960).
Junzo Inagaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He held the post of section chief (課長) at Otani University.

Juri Lotman (1922–1993) was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and its Faculty of Philology between 1939 and 1961, and held a post at the University of Tartu starting in 1954.

Jurij Andreevič Smirnov (1923–1984) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Military Institute of Foreign Languages (c. 1949–1954) and became a scientific researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1967.

Shigeaki Watanabe is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held a post at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and served as a professor at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was an adjunct lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and held a post at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Justin Edwards Abbott (1853–1932) was a scholar of Indology. He earned an A.B. at Dartmouth College (c. 1872–1876) and pursued studies at Union Theological Seminary (c. 1876–1879).
Justin Fifield works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He received an MA from the University of Texas at Austin in 2008 and was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University (attested 2009–2015).

Justin Hartley Moore (1884–1962) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Ph.D. at Columbia University (c. 1904–1908) under A. V. Williams Jackson and David P. Jackson. He taught French and Romanic languages at CCNY (1908, 1916).

Justin McDaniel (b. 1972) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He was an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and was appointed Edmund J. and Louise W. Kahn Endowed Professor of the Humanities at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2026).

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard (2003–2010) under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett. He has held positions at Oberlin College, the University of Miami, Dharma Drum Mountain, and Academia Sinica.
